title: A Reduced-Order Proof of Concept for AI-Guided Scenario-Criticality Search and VVUQ in  a Battery-Electric Rail Vehicle Cell Digital Twin
content: The “Daydreaming Factory” is a conceptual framework in which a digital model is used to explore future operating scenarios before they occur. It has not been given a formal mathematical form or an executed demonstration of its central algorithmic claim, that AI-guided search finds reliability-critical scenarios more efficiently than manual or random exploration. This paper gives a reduced-order, single-cell instantiation for a battery-electric rail vehicle (BERV) Li-ion cell, using equivalent-circuit and ageing parameters previously identified from NASA PCoE data. We define a four-dimensional scenario space (current stress, resistive fault, ageing-rate stress, initial state of charge) and a criticality score that includes a battery-management-system (BMS) overcurrent trip, which makes the landscape discontinuous: the worst case lies just below the trip point, not at the corner of the space. Differential evolution (DE) found a score of 7.867 with 1,345 evaluations, matching an exhaustive 390,625-point grid (7.847) at 0.34% of its cost, whereas random search with the same budget reached 7.447 ± 0.178 over ten trials. A coarse-versus-fine time-step check gave perfect rank agreement (Spearman ρ = Kendall τ = 1.000), although this is a weak test. The landscape and its constants are assumptions of this study, and DE was run once. The work is an algorithmic proof of concept, not a validated vehicle-level system.
